title: Dual-write consistency prober and automated rollback playbook for Jaeger/Tempo backend migrations
creator: Linh Nguyen
description: When migrating tenants (or entire clusters) from Jaeger to Tempo we need a low-friction, observable, and reversible migration path. This work implements a dual-write consistency prober that runs alongside dual-write deployments to detect span/trace divergences, and an automated rollback playbook (runbook + automation hooks) to safely revert consumer-facing routing when divergence or latency regressions exceed thresholds. The goal is zero data-loss migrations and quick, auditable rollback in case of functional or perf regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A cron / k8s job (trace-consistency-prober) that samples spans from the application side and validates presence and key attributes in both Jaeger and Tempo for a configurable tenant set is deployed to staging and runs successfully for 48h without false positives.
Mismatch metric tracing.migration.dual_write_mismatch_rate is emitted and dashboarded; alerts created for sustained mismatch_rate > 0.3% for > 15m.
Automated rollback playbook exists: a runbook in Confluence, an SRE-approved script that flips routing in the proxy layer (or routing policy) with canary gating and an idempotent safety check.
Playbook automation has a dry-run mode and requires two approvals for production rollback; all rollbacks are logged to audit S3 and emit tracing.migration.rollback_executed.
End-to-end integration test that seeds synthetic traces and verifies prober detects mismatches and that the rollback script toggles routing as expected in a staging environment.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy prober to staging for two days (sampling 1% of traces). 2) Validate metrics and reduce false positives by tuning attribute matchers. 3) Announce dual-write window and run prober in preprod for 48h at 5% sampling. 4) Enable dual-write in production for small tenant cohort (10 tenants) and monitor 72h. 5) Gradually increase cohort while monitoring mismatch_rate and latency. 6) If mismatch_rate OR P95 latency regressions exceed thresholds for > 15 minutes, follow automated rollback playbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for matching logic: attribute normalization, trace ID canonicalization, and time-window matching.
Integration test: synthetic trace generator writes to both Jaeger and Tempo and asserts prober behavior.
Chaos test: kill tempo ingesters and verify prober alerts and that rollback playbook prevents downstream impact.
Load test: run prober at production sampling rates against a copy of recent traffic (redacted) to validate costs and performance impact.
dashboards_to_update: Latency/Error dashboards that include tracing.backend.p95 and tracing.backend.error_rate
risks: False positives from attribute normalization mismatches leading to unnecessary rollbacks.
Prober overhead causing increased ingestion or noise on backends if sampling is misconfigured.
Edge-cases where spans are transformed differently by backends (tag renames, dropped logs) and cannot be matched deterministically.
Automation misfire: rollback script toggles routing during a transient downstream outage causing additional disruption.
